backup.production_rule: Wi-Fi password lockdown (s141). 20261209000000 adds one RESTRICTIVE select policy on public.app_settings, app_settings_wifi_password_closed_anon, for the anon role with key <> wifi_password, so the public key can no longer read the guest Wi-Fi password row directly. Every other key anon could read stays readable (wifi_ssid included); authenticated staff reads, admin writes, service_role and the SECURITY DEFINER functions guide_secrets_v1 and get_public_settings are unchanged. It stops (55000) if app_settings is missing or has row level security off. No table, column, grant, function or stored row changes.
backup.notes: restore_point and verified_at are placeholders: restamp them with a fresh backup at apply time (scripts/migrations/fill-restore-point.mjs). The migration carries no begin/commit (the runner wraps it); the rollback carries its own. Rehearse with migration-rehearsal-on-host.sh and the pgTAP suite s141_wifi_password_closed_anon before the apply.

forward_verification.name: policy_is_restrictive_select_for_anon
forward_verification.query: select count(*) = 1 from pg_policies where schemaname = 'public' and tablename = 'app_settings' and policyname = 'app_settings_wifi_password_closed_anon' and permissive = 'RESTRICTIVE' and cmd = 'SELECT' and roles = array['anon']::name[]

forward_verification.name: rls_is_on_for_app_settings
forward_verification.query: select relrowsecurity from pg_class where oid = 'public.app_settings'::regclass

rollback.safe_until: any time; it only drops the one policy (after it, anon can read the wifi_password row again)

feature_flags.name: no_flag_the_guide_reads_the_password_through_guide_secrets_v1
feature_flags.required_state: None. No live front-end reads wifi_password as anon any more (guide v9 hands it out against a guest token).

compatibility.evidence: Not yet rehearsed: run migration-rehearsal-on-host.sh on a restored copy and the pgTAP suite s141_wifi_password_closed_anon (22 assertions), then record the result here.
